name: 07_lambda_ceiling_saturated_sorts_last
description: CROSS-CORE guard on the λ FINITE CEILING (MAX_LAMBDA = 1e300). A runaway step on a pool far over cap drives λ to +∞ without the clamp; since resolve SKIPS a non-finite weight (`if w.is_finite()`), a +∞-priced (maximally saturated) option would score as FREE and sort to the FRONT — the exact INVERSION of the intended shed. With the clamp, λ pins to the finite ceiling 1e300 and the saturated option sorts LAST. Pool `p` has cap 0 and step α=1e300; a single tick with usage 1e10 gives next = 1e300·(1e10−0) = 1e310, which OVERFLOWS f64 to +∞ — the genuine runaway the clamp must catch. Without the is_finite()/MAX_LAMBDA clamp `next>0 ? next : 0` stores +∞ and resolve routes `saturated` FREE to the FRONT; with the clamp λ pins to MAX_LAMBDA = 1e300 (finite). This input is chosen so the golden is NON-VACUOUS: it actually overflows, so removing the clamp flips the queue (verified). Option `saturated` draws 1 unit on `p` (financial 0) → score λ·1 = 1e300; `rival` is priced financial 1.0 → score 1.0. So rival leads and saturated trails. expectedLambda.p == 1e300 (FINITE — never +∞), expectedOrder == [rival, saturated]. Captured from the live tick→publish→resolve on both cores.
